The four necessary conditions for deadlock in this problem are as follows:

  1. Mutual Exclusion: Only one philosopher can use a chopstick at a time.

  3. No Preemption: Once a philosopher has picked up a chopstick, they cannot be forced to give it up.
  4. Circular Wait: Philosophers wait for each other in a circular pattern, each one waiting for the chopstick held by the philosopher to their left.

All four of these conditions hold in the dining philosophers problem. A deadlock can occur when all five philosophers hold one chopstick and wait for the other chopstick, resulting in a circular wait.

One way to avoid deadlocks is to eliminate the Circular Wait condition. This can be done by implementing a locking mechanism that assigns chopsticks in a defined order, so that no two philosophers can pick up chopsticks that would result in a circular wait. For example, a philosopher can only pick up the chopstick to their left if they don't already have the chopstick to their right.
